brief.subject: Fake passport help sites and a debt relief scam aimed at seniors
brief.headline: FTC Targets Fake Passport Help Sites and a Debt Relief Scheme That Hit Seniors
brief.dek: Regulators sued alleged passport-service impostors, won a $106.8 million judgment in a debt relief case, and accused Dollar General of overcharging.
brief.lede: The FTC says some passport help sites pose as the government through paid search ads. Before paying anyone for passport services, confirm you are on an official government site.

sections.heading: Passport 'Help' Sites Posing as Government
bullets: The FTC sued GovAssist LLC, Entry LLC and Scott Zuckerman over an alleged government impersonation scheme involving passport services.
Regulators say the operation used deceptive paid search ads, so the top search result may not be the government.
The complaint also cites misleading promises and fake reviews, so glowing ratings alone are no proof a site is legitimate.
Check that a passport site is official before entering personal details or paying any fee.

sections.heading: Debt Relief Scheme Hit Seniors and Veterans
bullets: A federal court permanently banned operators of an alleged debt relief scheme that targeted seniors and veterans.
The FTC says the operators pretended to be banks, credit card companies and government agencies to win trust.
On October 14, 2026, the court entered a $106.8 million default judgment against the corporate defendants.
Unsolicited debt relief offers that claim to come from your bank or a government agency deserve extra suspicion.

sections.heading: Dollar General Accused of Register Overcharges
bullets: The FTC and 20 states sued Dollar General, alleging register prices routinely exceeded shelf tags and advertised prices.
Regulators say the practice ran for years and cost consumers millions of dollars.
Compare your receipt against shelf prices before leaving, especially on larger purchases.
